title: 2011 AMC 12A Problem 11
statement: Circles \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) each have radius \(1.\) Circles \(A\) and \(B\) share one point of tangency. Circle \(C\) has a point of tangency with the midpoint of \(\overline{AB}.\) What is the area inside circle \(C\) but outside circle \(A\) and circle \(B?\)

solutions.text:
Place \(A = (-1, 0),\) \(B = (1, 0),\) so their tangency point is the origin, the midpoint of \(\overline{AB}.\) Then \(C = (0, 1),\) since \(C\) passes through the origin.

The distance from \(C\) to \(A\) (and to \(B\)) is \(\sqrt2.\) Two unit circles whose centers are \(\sqrt2\) apart overlap in a lens of area \[ \begin{aligned} 2\cos^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\right) \\ {}- \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\sqrt{4 - 2} \\ = 2 \cdot \tfrac{\pi}{4} - 1 = \tfrac{\pi}{2} - 1. \end{aligned} \]

Circles \(A\) and \(B\) meet only at the origin, so the two lenses do not overlap. The wanted area is \[ \pi - 2\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - 1\right) = 2. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Place the centers at \(A(-1,0),\) \(B(1,0),\) and \(C(0,1);\) the distance from \(C\) to each of \(A, B\) is \(\sqrt2\)
The wanted area is the area of \(C\) minus the two lens-shaped overlaps of \(C\) with \(A\) and with \(B\)
